messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
At 10 kPa the melting (freezing) point of pure water is only slightly below the standard 0 °C.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice–water equilibrium:

\[
\frac{dT}{dP}\;=\;\frac{\Delta V}{\Delta S}
\]

where  

* \(\Delta V \approx 8.3\times10^{-5}\,\text{m}^3/\text{mol}\) (difference between liquid and solid volumes)  
* \(\Delta S \approx 22\,\text{J}/(\text{mol·K})\)

gives \(dT/dP \approx 3.8\times10^{-6}\,\text{K/Pa}\).

From 1 atm (101.3 kPa) to 10 kPa the pressure change is \(-91.3\) kPa, so

\[
\Delta T \approx 3.8\times10^{-6}\,\text{K/Pa}\times(-91,300\,\text{Pa})
          \approx -0.35\,\text{K}.
\]

Thus the freezing point at 10 kPa is roughly

\[
T_{\text{freeze}} \approx 0\,^\circ\text{C} - 0.35\,^\circ\text{C}
                    \approx -0.35\,^\circ\text{C}.
\]

So water freezes at about **–0.3 °C** under a pressure of 10 kPa.
